chapter: Los Angeles bands and theater pits, 1927-30
title: Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club
summary: Redd asks about the Sebastian Cotton Club; Blakeney says it was the best job in Los Angeles short of the theaters.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, tell us a little bit about the Sebastian Cotton
Club; Frank Sebastian, I think, is very significant.
Is that not where Bing Crosby and the trio that he was singing with once worked?
I think you're talking about the Biltmore, also the Coconut Grove.
Did the Les Hite Orchestra work there for Frank Sebastian?
Oh, yes, sure Les worked there.
That was a pretty important club at that time.
It was the best job we had in Los Angeles. If you worked the Cotton Club, we couldn't get a better job, except the theaters. I think the Burbank Theater and the Follies Theater.
